headlines.title: State Street Utilities SPDR (XLU) Sells NextEra and Southern on Nov. 5
headlines.summary: The fund sold $384.5 million of stock, cutting all 31 positions and adding nothing.

headlines.title: What Southern (SO) Said on Its Q3 Earnings Call
headlines.summary: Southern (NYSE:SO) expects to exceed its original 2026 adjusted earnings guidance after third-quarter results benefited from warmer weather, growing electricity use and rising demand from large customers, including data centers. The utility reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.

headlines.title: NextEra Energy vs. Southern Company: Which Dividend Stock Is Better for Retirement?
headlines.summary: Both utilities just beat earnings estimates and both are cashing in on data center demand. But one has faster growth while the other has the steadier paycheck, and retirees have to decide which of those matters more.

headlines.title: Is Southern (SO) Still A Bargain Or Fully Priced On Earnings?
headlines.summary: Southern Company has rewarded long term holders. With the stock trading around earnings that markets are constantly repricing, the key issue is whether today’s valuation still lines up with what the utility is actually earning. Over the past 5 years, Southern has delivered a 77.2% total return, which puts real weight on the question of how much earnings power is now already reflected in the share price.

headlines.title: Are Wall Street Analysts Bullish on Southern Company Stock?
headlines.summary: Southern Company has underperformed the broader market over the past year, and analysts remain unsure about the stock’s prospects.

description: The Southern Company, through its subsidiaries, engages in the sale of electricity. The company offers electric service to retail customers and wholesale customers; and energy-related products and services to natural gas choice markets. It also develops, constructs, acquires, owns, operates, and manages power generation assets, as well as battery energy storage projects; sells electricity at market-based rates in the wholesale market; and deploys microgrids for commercial, industrial, governmental, and utility customers. In addition, the company is involved in the distribution of natural gas in Illinois, Georgia, Virginia, and Tennessee; distributes energy and resilience solutions; and invests in telecommunications. The Southern Company was incorporated in 1945 and is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia.
